extracted.intended_audience: Authors (mathematicians) preparing manuscripts, graphics, and source files for submission to American Mathematical Society (AMS) journals, Memoirs, proceedings, or monographs
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and technical requirements and quality standards for preparing, formatting, and submitting manuscripts, graphics, and source files to AMS publications (journals, Memoirs, proceedings, monographs). Covers LaTeX/AMS-TEX usage, graphics specs, metadata, and submission methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule line weight minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: If a rule line is gray or colored, its weight should be no thinner than 1 point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid “hairline” weight as it will be nearly invisible at high resolution and may disappear in printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graded line weight increments
rubrics_metrics.description: Graded line weights should increase in increments of at least 0.5pt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increments less than 0.5pt are insufficiently distinguishable at high resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screened fill percentages
rubrics_metrics.description: Screened fills should be screened not less than 15% and not greater than 85%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Less than 15% will print as white; greater than 85% will print as black.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text in graphics as outlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Text included in graphics files should be font outlines rather than bitmaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AMS typesets on a high-resolution imagesetter; bitmaps at 300 dpi or less may appear poor next to high-resolution text. If bitmapped characters are part of bitmapped line art files, they should be at 1200 dpi for ideal output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-electronic graphics quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonelectronic graphics should be drawn in black ink with clean, unbroken lines on nonabsorbent paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whenever possible, fonts used in graphics should match those used in the text. Authors’ original graphics are used whenever possible. Send originals of photographs/electronic artwork; do not use paper clips or staples; use cardboard backing; do not fold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission formats for color images
rubrics_metrics.description: For a color image (converted to B/W or to appear in color), submit one of: glossy color photograph, color transparency or interneg, or color slide (listed in order of preference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use glossy color photograph first, then transparency/interneg, then slide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color graphics print/electronic behavior and resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS normally does not include color graphics in print version; color submitted will appear in color in electronic version as submitted. If color is warranted by Editor and Publisher, color figures should have resolution of at least 300 pixels per inch for photographic images and 600 pixels per inch for line art when printed at 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally supply in EPS format; TIFF and JPEG are also acceptable. Note: PostScript is not the same as Encapsulated PostScript (EPS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Displayed equations formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Check displayed equations carefully, making sure they are broken and aligned following AMS guidelines, and that they do not exceed the width of the page for the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multi-line displays use the structures defined in the amsmath user's guide or appropriate references ([ALG], [Sp]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: For AMS journals, initial electronic submissions via the AMS peer-review submission web page; nonelectronic submissions: send one copy of the manuscript to Centralized Manuscript Processing with clear indication of intended journal and contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See www.ams.org/peer-review-submission for electronic instructions; include email or postal contact info on nonelectronic submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed macro packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Only 'public' macro packages (packages available from CTAN) may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input only public macro packages from CTAN; other macro definitions must be embedded in the preamble and every electronic file must be processable independently with all macros included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macro definition practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Macros should be defined with \newcommand, not with \def (for AMS-LATEX); for AMS-TEX use \define rather than \def.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use \def; do not redeﬁne any existing LaTeX, AMS-LATEX, or AMS-TEX commands. If a macro name already exists, choose another name instead of redefining.

rubrics_metrics.name: No camera-ready submissions for journals/memoirs
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals (and Memoirs) do not accept camera-ready submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Camera-ready rules differ for certain series — check specific author package and handbook sections if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redefine existing commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not redeﬁne any existing LATEX, AMS-LATEX, or AMS-TEX commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use package-provided structuring commands; avoid redefining standard macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperref handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The hyperref package will be added by Providence staff at the appropriate stage of the production process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not include hyperref for production; hyperref will be applied to internal cross-references and external URLs by staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supplied template and document style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the template supplied in the author package for your particular publication and the appropriate document style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author packages include templates and sample files; using these reduces production time and errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not modify page sizes or dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not modify page sizes or other dimensions; page sizes must conform to the specifications for the journal or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dimensions are publication-specific; altering them can cause production problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: No author-defined macros in certain metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic manuscripts, do not use author-defined macros in author names, titles, abstracts, section headings, or references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metadata fields must be plain and processable; avoid custom macros there.

rubrics_metrics.name: First page title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The first page must contain a descriptive title that is short but informative; avoid vague phrases like 'some remarks about' or 'concerning'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply a shortened form of the title if the full title is too long for the running head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title capitalization and math in title
rubrics_metrics.description: In article titles, only the first word and proper nouns should be capitalized. Avoid the use of TeX math in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of TeX math coding (especially dollar signs) will result in inaccurate bibliographic listings; provide a short title for running head if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running head formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Running heads on left-hand (even) pages should have the author name(s) in uppercase letters and must match the names on the first page; shortened forms allowed if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uppercasing will be applied automatically when using AMS style files; leave room for page number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS journal articles (except Book Reviews) must contain an abstract whose main purpose is to enable readers to absorb the nature and results of the article quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should contain no text references to the bibliography unless the bibliographic reference is fully supplied (e.g., 'Author (2005)'). May be multiple paragraphs and include displayed material. Suggested upper limit: about 150 words for short papers, 300 words for long papers (300 suggested for Memoirs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics Subject Classification (MSC) numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification numbers representing the primary and secondary subjects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list is available at www.ams.org/msc/ and primary classification numbers must appear (required in unmarked, unnumbered footnotes on the first/abstract page as specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant and acknowledgement metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Give information on grants or contracts under which the research was performed, including grant number, using \thanks in an electronic manuscript; unmarked, unnumbered footnotes on the first page should include primary classification numbers (required); grant information (optional); and keywords/phrases (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting is automatic when using AMS style files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author affiliations and addresses placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic or other affiliations should appear at the end of your article, after the bibliography or references. A current address (if different) should follow the affiliation on a separate line. An email address should be included if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses are part of the topmatter in AMS author packages; formatting is handled automatically by the style files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic data inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: All bibliographic data must be incorporated into the article file. If using BibTeX, insert the contents of the .bbl file into your .tex file; do not send the .bib file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include complete reference information and use \cite in the manuscript. Use AMS abbreviations for journals and series from [ASMR].

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics margin and conformance
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that any graphics do not extend into the margin; allowable width may vary depending on journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphics must also conform to AMS graphics guidelines (check the Graphics guidelines document at www.ams.org/authors). Verify resolution and file formats per graphics specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread your work carefully before submitting it to the AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author-prepared publications will not be given an editorial proofreading; author-prepared camera-ready submissions are not proofread at AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A Consent to Publish and Copyright Agreement is sent to the author(s) when the accepted paper is received at the AMS; the signed form should be returned to Production immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain rights to use all or part of their own work in future publications, but AMS may request transfer of some rights. If copyright is transferred, authors may dedicate paper to the public domain after 28 years from publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoirs-specific chapter/titles rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoirs articles: ordinarily every chapter must begin on a new right-hand (odd-numbered) page. In chapter titles, capitalize the first and last words and all nouns, pronouns, adjectives, adverbs, and verbs; lowercase articles, conjunctions, and prepositions except when first or last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Memoirs author package and Memoirs checklist. Running heads: left-hand pages show chapter title in uppercase; right-hand pages show section title in uppercase; shorten only if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author package usage recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare articles and monographs using the appropriate AMS author package to reduce cost and shorten publication time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author packages contain sample papers, templates for topmatter, the handbook, instructions, and style files. Use the appropriate package for your publication type (journal, monograph, proceedings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required software versions and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: To use an author package you must have TEX and Computer Modern fonts; for AMS-LATEX you need LATEX 2e (no earlier than June 1995), AMS-LATEX, AMSFonts, and the appropriate author package; for AMS-TEX you need TEX (plain format), AMS-TEX (including amsppt.sty), AMSFonts, and the appropriate author package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current AMS-LATEX author packages will run only under LATEX 2e or later. Some author packages are available only for AMS-LATEX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author package retrieval and installation
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain author packages from the AMS web server (monographs/proceedings/journals). Every author package is available as a .zip file or as separate files; retrieve all files and install style files in appropriate TEX directories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot use .zip, retrieve every file. Install AMS-LATEX style files where amsart.cls, amsproc.cls, and amsbook.cls are located; AMS-TEX style files where amsppt.sty is located.

rubrics_metrics.name: File preparation and testing steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Print the README, change the document style in sample *.tex files to use the package retrieved, TEX and print the output, and print the .pdf files unless you already have copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided sample and template files to check your setup before preparing your submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding organization and reuse of macros
rubrics_metrics.description: Put definitions for frequently occurring mathematical expressions together in the preamble; once a macro is created, use it consistently for every occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AMS style file commands to identify important features (sections, theorems) rather than defining new structural commands. Use TEX coding for special fonts only within the manuscript text, not in headings or predefined environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use TeX coding for line/page breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic manuscripts do not use TeX coding to control line and page breaks; explicit horizontal and vertical spacing commands should be avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lines and pages may break differently in production; inserted breaks will have to be removed and may introduce errors. For camera-ready submissions, check line/page breaks following paging guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready submission file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For camera-ready submissions submit DVI and/or PostScript or PDF file(s) along with all related TEX and Encapsulated PostScript graphics files. The TEX file will be archived and work will be printed directly from your output file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact AMS Technical Support if you want to submit the entire article in PostScript or PDF format; follow camera-ready specific paging guidelines in the handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted-file submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance, send source file(s) (TEX and any graphics files) and, if camera-ready, DVI/PS/PDF to the Providence office; files sent must be the EXACT files used to generate the accepted proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify the Checklist for electronic submissions. Send only files needed to process or archive the submission. For books send printed copy or PDF to Acquisitions; for journals send printed copy or PDF to the editor who forwards it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bundling multiple files
rubrics_metrics.description: If your submission consists of multiple files, bundle them using Zip so only one compressed file needs to be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bundling lessens the chance of name conflicts or file corruption. Use unique filenames to avoid overwrite problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred and acceptable transmission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred method for submitting bundled accepted manuscripts is the AMS web server; other acceptable methods are email (bundled and source files only), FTP, or on CD/diskette/flash drive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Web submission requires an AMS Web Account. For email submissions attach files, not inline; use pub-submit@ams.org. For FTP use ftp.ams.org incoming directory in binary mode and notify pub-submit@ams.org after transfer. For physical media label media and include identifying information; delete extraneous files before sending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textures/DVI handling note
rubrics_metrics.description: If files were created with Textures, extract the DVI file using the '.dvi' option and submit the DVI as part of the bundle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If electronic transmission impossible, send on CD or Macintosh disk and AMS will extract the DVI file.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS-LATEX and AMS-TEX basic structure commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the provided commands for structuring (\section, \subsection, \begin{figure} ... \includegraphics{filename} \caption{} \label{} etc.) and the theorem environment commands provided by AMS-LATEX/AMS-TEX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem styles: 'plain' for Theorem/Lemma/Corollary/etc.; 'definition' for Definition/Example/Algorithm; 'remark' for Remark/Note/Claim/etc. All \newtheorem specifications should be included in the preamble.
